dispositions.v012Title: cobre-io's policy checkpoint format is literally cut-records, exempt from the genericity gate

oracle.stdout: OK: no algorithm-specific vocabulary found in infrastructure crates.
reachLimits: the pattern matches `\bCut\b` with word boundaries: `printf 'PolicyCutRecord StageCutsPayload StageCuts' | grep -Eo '\bCut\b'` yields 0 matches, so CamelCase identifiers evade it
the scan is `find <crate>/src -name '*.rs'` over five src/ trees; `find crates/cobre-io/src -name '*.fbs'` returns 0, so crates/cobre-io/schemas/policy.fbs is never read

dispositions.changedSinceV012: The gate exemption is retired by the script itself: EXCLUDED_FILES=() at scripts/ci/check-infra-genericity.sh:74 and the gate exits 0 at the baseline over output/policy. The FlatBuffers table vocabulary moved to affine pieces (`table AffinePiece` crates/cobre-io/schemas/policy.fbs:105) and the provenance carrier is now the `CheckpointManifest` table / policy/manifest.bin (crates/cobre-io/schemas/policy.fbs:284; metadata.json retired). Exit 0 is NOT proof the claim retired (see oracle.reachLimits).
dispositions.survivingClaim: Cut vocabulary the oracle cannot see persists in production: `PolicyCutRecord` (crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/records.rs:98), `StageCutsPayload` (crates/cobre-io/src/output/policy/records.rs:176) and the `StageCuts` root table (crates/cobre-io/schemas/policy.fbs:140) — the persisted value-function format is still cut-shaped; the lexical exemption is gone, the structural coupling is not.
